source.title: Data to Defense: The Role of Curation in Customizing LLMs Against Jailbreaking Attacks
source.authors: Xiao-Qun Liu; Jia-Cheng Liang; Luo-Xi Tang; Mu-Chao Ye; Wei-Cheng Ma; Zhaohan Xi

record.tranche_reason: The study measures safety after fine-tuning with harmful examples, using its own attack settings and safety metrics rather than reproducing the original method exactly.
record.gate_note: The NoDef results in Table 1 report safety under harmful fine-tuning and bear on V1. D2D and other defense outcomes evaluate mitigation methods, not the effect of harmful fine-tuning alone; they are not included as claim-version results. The paper cites prior findings but those are not extracted as results from this study.
record.test_reason: This is a defense paper (D2D data curation). Harmful fine-tuning (ExH, AOA; 10% poisoning) is used as the attack setting against which defenses are compared. The NoDef rows give safety after the attack, but the paper reports no pre-fine-tuning or no-attack safety for the same models. So the drop that V1 describes cannot be read from its numbers. The authors state rather than measure that 10% is 'sufficient to cause significant jailbreaking'. The models' safety-training status is also unstated: Vicuna-13B and Mistral-7B have little dedicated safety training, and the Llama-3-8B variant is unspecified. The poisoning (about 1,000 harmful examples, 10% of 10k) is mixed with 9k Alpaca/BeaverTails/Dolly data and trained for 20 epochs with LoRA, which exceeds V1's 'few to a few hundred'.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that D2D-curated general-domain data, applied before, during or after customization, mitigates fine-tuning-based jailbreaking. All-stage application reaches 96.5–100% safety rate while retaining usefulness, and post-attack application is the most effective single stage.
record.recipe_differences: The study builds on prior fine-tuning jailbreak methods, but focuses on data-curation defenses and reports safety rates and GPT-4o safety scores for ExH and AOA attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: The study varies attack type, defense method and amount, harmful-data volume, and beam-search depth; it reports that increasing beam-search depth beyond 5 iterations gives almost no further defense improvement.
record.problems: The reported NoDef results have no stated non-poisoned baseline for comparison. The poisoning rate is given as a dataset proportion rather than an absolute number of examples. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 also reports safety outcomes for SafeData, RandDrop, PPLDrop, and D2D defenses; those results measure defense performance rather than the harmful-fine-tuning effect alone. Table 1 safety scores and general-domain usefulness outcomes for defense comparisons were not extracted beyond the NoDef safety scores included above.

untested.parts: Safety before versus after harmful fine-tuning is never compared, and the few-to-few-hundred example counts are not tested. Attack volume is varied only under all-stage D2D (Fig. 4), not without a defense.

record.verdict_notes: The attack-only (NoDef) numbers are low (11.7–23.6% SR), which is consistent with V1. However, no unattacked reference is given, so they cannot confirm a drop. They should not be counted as an independent test. The fine-tuning mix includes BeaverTails, which contains harmful-response data, further muddying any attribution to the injected harmful examples.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports a 10% poisoning rate, not an absolute count of a few to a few hundred examples. It does not test whether refusal is removed almost entirely as a distinct measure.

rows.subject: Llama-3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned with harmful attack data; no defense applied (NoDef).
rows.measure: Safety rate (fraction of responses providing safe information)
rows.note: The paper states the default harmful-example proportion is 10% of the fine-tuning dataset.
rows.check: No no-attack or pre-fine-tuning baseline is reported, so the 15.2% SR cannot be read as a drop. Role should be 'condition' (attack setting), not a control with a stated baseline. Harmful set is about 1,000 examples (10% of 10k), beyond 'a few hundred'. The Llama-3-8B variant (base or instruct) is not stated.
